deviation_start_frame.what: Every animation was made with directions ["east"] and the Husk's SOUTH rotation passed as custom_start_frame_url: for the Peeling that is ART's exemplar art/anchors/husk-peeling-64.png, for the Nutshell the Step 1 base. The descriptions are as written ("toward the right").
deviation_start_frame.why: Both east rotations lost the core. The Peeling's east rotation is redesigned into a 28x32 open hook with no core (target 22x18); the Nutshell's turned the crack and core to its right edge, leaving a 1-2 px speck. Every east animation starts from its rotation, so all of them would have started coreless.
deviation_start_frame.decided_by: David, 2026-10-16, after the job stopped and asked (Step 3 was not started before the answer). His rule for the rest: a frame that loses the core is not a retake on its own (ART paints the core back); retake only for the wrong action or the Husk redesigned.
deviation_start_frame.kept: peeling/rotation-east.png and nutshell/rotation-east.png (and rotation/<dir>.png for all four directions) are kept as delivered, unused.

arguments.description: A Nutshell Husk: a big squat hollow nut-shaped double shell, about 40 px wide and 34 px tall, resting heavily on the ground. The thick ridged outer shell is pale and translucent (white to lavender), cracked along the front; through the crack the smoother inner shell shows, and inside it one small bright pale-yellow core with a dark ring. No face, eyes, mouth or legs. Top-down RPG pixel art seen from a low three-quarter view, light from the top left, a 1 px dark violet outline, two or three shades per material, no dithering, transparent background, no text or letters.

reference_images.usage: enemy style: the same hollow pale shell, translucent lavender shade, core and ring, outline
scale only: this is the player, 45 px tall; the Husk sits beside it

step1_nutshell_base.max_colors: not passed (the job names only the palette)
step1_nutshell_base.pick_why: Of the four candidates whose core shows (0, 4, 8, 15), 0 is closest to 40x34: exactly 40 wide, 47 tall (4: 42x49, 8: 47x52, 15: 48x48). Every one of the 16 is 39-52 px tall, so none reaches 34; no retake, because candidates with a visible core exist. The core sits in a dark vertical slit, which on all four reads somewhat like an eye.
step1_nutshell_base.placement: candidate 0 moved down 1 row (lowest pixel 52 -> 53), columns unchanged (12-51, already centred); pixels identical, nothing scaled or recoloured
